title: A conservator leaves the varnish in place
bodyMd: When conservator Ines Baptista began cleaning an eighteenth-century painted ceiling, she expected to find a single layer of varnish. Instead she uncovered four, each brushed on by a different restorer over two centuries. Rather than stripping them all away, Baptista removed only the topmost layer and left the other three, a decision that struck several of her colleagues as excessively ______. Baptista replied that every layer she took off destroyed evidence that future researchers might one day need.
accessibilityText: A short passage with a blank to fill. Conservator Ines Baptista expected one layer of varnish on an eighteenth-century painted ceiling but found four, each added by a different restorer over two centuries. She removed only the top layer and left the other three. Several colleagues thought this decision was excessively blank. Baptista answered that every layer she removed destroyed evidence future researchers might need. The blank appears near the end of the fourth sentence, after the word "excessively".
